association_citations.quote:
3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：C2-SA、C3-NaDFP-TMSB-NB。

### 候选资料：C2-SA（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride；添加剂用量：2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec4]：2.1. Preparation of the batteries
Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. A baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving NaPF $_6$ (1 mol/L) into a mixed solvent of EC and EMC (weight ratio 3:7). To formulate a functional electrolyte, 1 wt% 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) was added to the baseline system. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode active materials were procured from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode slurry consisted of 94.5 wt% NFM, 1.8 wt% PVDF, 1 wt% carbon nanotubes (CNT), 2.5 wt% Super P, and 0.2 wt% maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP), and was cast onto aluminum foil. The HC anode was composed of 95 wt% HC,

![](images/8bfcb630e9de984c98fbfc69f2dd0cb440e9bd8293373fa0ec9806e9fb6d55de.jpg)  
Fig. 1. 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) is introduced as electrolyte additive to enhance the electrochemical performance of pouch SIBs.

1.5 wt% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2 wt% styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 wt% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd.) was employed as the separator. The areal mass loadings of the cathode and anode were 33.0 and 20.1 mg/cm $^{2}$ , respectively, with a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.1 (based on theoretical capacity calculation). The dry pouch cells were evacuated at 80 °C for 72 h, transferred into an argon-filled glovebox, and injected with 6.0 g of electrolyte. All other fabrication procedures followed standard practices in battery assembly.

### 候选资料：C3-NaDFP-TMSB-NB（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：NaDFP, TMSB；添加剂用量：NaDFP:TMSB=1:1.5 (ratio only; absolute wt% not stated in the main text)。
- 配方原文 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4]：2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the HC anode. The areal loading of the anode and cathode were 16.0 g m $^{-2}$ and 33.0 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The semi-finished pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.
